overall.sentence: Gate-controlled loading of localized quasiparticles that produces interferometric phase slips was shown earlier in a GaAs Mach-Zehnder interferometer (arXiv:2410.16488), and bulk e/4 quasiparticles were inferred earlier in a bilayer-graphene Fabry-Pérot interferometer (arXiv:2412.19886); what is new here is a dedicated anti-dot gate inside a bilayer-graphene Fabry-Pérot cavity, used across five fractional states including the even-denominator 1+1/2.

assessment.claim: Headline: highly controlled tuning of localized anyon populations with a gate-defined anti-dot integrated into a bilayer-graphene FPI (claim 1)
assessment.note: Ghosh et al. (cited [54]) already used a small charged top gate in the interferometer bulk to induce localized quasiparticles and periodic phase slips (question and method match, GaAs MZI); Kim et al. 2402.12432 (cited [12]) saw phase jumps from quasiparticle addition in a BLG FPI but by filling deviation, not a local gate. New here: a local anti-dot gate in a BLG FPI.

assessment.claim: Direct measurement of localized charge e/4 at 1+1/2; controlling the population of localized e/4 anyons in an interferometer is a milestone (claims 4 and 5)
assessment.note: Kim et al. (cited [13]) already inferred e/4 bulk quasiparticles in a BLG FPI at half filling by controlled filling deviation (question and system match); new here is one-by-one loading by an anti-dot gate and slip-size and slip-count estimates of the charge.

assessment.claim: Slip regions recur once per anti-dot Landau level, pointing to reconstructed anti-dot edges; 'previously unexplored aspects of localized quasiparticles' (claim 6)
assessment.note: Röösli et al. tied interferometer phase jumps to changing quasiparticle number with edge reconstruction in a GaAs quantum dot (integer regime), and Di Luca et al. 2504.16750 studied antidot-edge coupling in a BLG antidot without an FPI; no earlier paper found with recurring AD Landau-level slip regions in a fractional BLG FPI, but these searches were thin on this claim, so it is not graded no_precedent_found.

positioning: The paper sits between GaAs work that used a gate inside an interferometer to add localized quasiparticles (Ghosh et al., 2410.16488, Mach-Zehnder) and bilayer-graphene Fabry-Pérot work that inferred bulk e/4 quasiparticles by tuning the cavity filling (Kim et al., 2412.19886); its addition is a local anti-dot gate in a BLG Fabry-Pérot cavity that loads quasiparticles one by one in five fractional states, including the even-denominator 1+1/2, plus the per-Landau-level recurrence of slip regions. A closely matching study, Kim et al. 'Selective braiding of different anyons in the even-denominator fractional quantum Hall effect' (2603.11162), reports a BLG Fabry-Pérot interferometer with an embedded antidot, braiding phases pi and pi/2 at half filling, and was posted the same day as this paper, so it is concurrent rather than prior and calls for no item here, but referees will very likely ask for a comparison. No earlier paper contradicts an explicit priority statement; the two items are about positioning and one strong word. Sources: the paper's reference list and 8 arXiv API queries (9 successful calls, none failed).

issues.claim: Headline: gate-controlled tuning of localized anyon populations in a BLG FPI
issues.headline: Position the anti-dot approach against the earlier GaAs gate experiment
issues.issue: Ghosh et al. (arXiv:2410.16488, cited as [54]) already used a small charged gate inside an interferometer to induce localized quasiparticles and periodic phase slips, with the expected slip size at 1/3 and deviating slip direction at 2/5 and 3/7. The introduction describes this work only as phase slips 'in a subset' of states, which undersells it and leaves the contribution here unpositioned against the closest earlier experiment.

evidence.quote: Recently, a larger AD was placed in an optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer in GaAs, leading to the observation of phase slips only in a subset of the measured abelian FQH states [54, 55].

issues.fix: Describe what [54] showed accurately and state what is added here: a local anti-dot gate in a BLG Fabry-Pérot cavity, five fractional states, and the even-denominator 1+1/2 state.

edit.before: Recently, a larger AD was placed in an optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer in GaAs, leading to the observation of phase slips only in a subset of the measured abelian FQH states [54, 55].
edit.after: Recently, a small charged gate in the bulk of an optical-like Mach-Zehnder interferometer in GaAs was used to induce localized quasiparticles and periodic phase slips, whose size matched the expected braiding phase at ν = 1/3 while their direction deviated at 2/5 and 3/7 [54, 55]. Here we bring such local gate control to a BLG Fabry-Pérot interferometer and extend it to even-denominator states.

issues.claim: Direct measurement of localized charge e/4 at 1+1/2
issues.headline: Soften 'direct measurement' of e/4; earlier BLG work inferred it
issues.issue: Kim et al. (arXiv:2412.19886, cited as [13]) already inferred bulk e/4 quasiparticles in a BLG Fabry-Pérot interferometer at half filling. The paper credits this in Section IV, but the introduction calls its own e/4 result a 'direct measurement' that 'culminates' the work, which is stronger than needed given that the charge here is also inferred, from slip size and spacing with an assumed anti-dot radius.

evidence.quote: culminating in the direct measurement of charge |e∗loc /e| = 1/4 for the presumed non-abelian anyon quasiparticles in even-denominator states.

issues.fix: Replace 'direct measurement' with wording that reflects the inference and cite [13] at this point.
